_comment: Week 12 trajectory eval: 13 cases, each a VIEW on an eval case (same question, same IDE version), plus the tool path a correct agent should take. Written by reasoning from the corpus BEFORE the agent was scored on it. A trajectory is the sequence of NEEDS (search / exists / lifecycle / verify) in the order the agent issued them, consecutive repeats collapsed (several calls in one lap are parallel). `accepted` lists every legitimate sequence: the sweep at the end is optional only where the final code or text touches no symbol with a lifecycle event.

cases.why: plain how-to on 2.4: find a sample + docs, verify the sample, then check lifecycle of what it uses
plain how-to on 3.0: same path; nothing in 3.0 is deprecated so a missing sweep is also fine
names a method and asks about 3.0: existence at 3.0, lifecycle, upgrade info + sample + docs, verify the replacement's sample
a method that never existed: check it, find the nearest real name's docs; no sample, no lifecycle of the unknown name
factual: existence + lifecycle of the named method, one docs search; no sample to verify
asks whether an argument is removed: existence + lifecycle, then migration info, a replacement sample, verify
major version only: still search, verify and sweep
no version anywhere: NO tool at all, ask the caller
plain how-to on 2.4 whose sample uses arguments removed in 3.0: the sweep is REQUIRED
version inferred from an error message, then existence + lifecycle of the missing method, search, verify
a 2.1 caller asks for something 2.1 cannot do: search finds nothing relevant, so nothing to verify and nothing to sweep
a pasted secret changes nothing about the path
